newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi intensifies border patrols.
newsitem.headline: Saudi intensifies border patrols.

text.p: Saudi Arabia will from Monday step up its patrols of land and sea borders in a crackdown on smugglers and infiltrators, a Saudi newspaper said on Monday.

"In implementation of orders by Interior Minister Prince Nayef the border guards start from Monday intensifying their border patrols and doubling their presence on land border points and Jeddah port (on the Red Sea) to close loopholes for... smugglers and infiltrators," the Okaz daily said.

It quoted the commander of the border guards, Brigadier General Talal bin Mohsen Anqawi, as saying the border guards would ... "take all measures, double efforts and intensify security patrols to form a security fence" along the borders.
It did not give other details or state the reason for the new measures. in the world's largest oil producer and exporter.

Saudi Arabia, which occupies most of the Arabian peninsula between the Red Sea and the Gulf, shares land borders with Jordan, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Yemen. It is connected to the Gulf island state of Bahrain by a causeway.

Four Saudi men who confessed on state television last year to being behind the November 1995 bombing of a U.S. military training centre in Riyadh said they had smuggled some of the explosives from Yemen.
They were beheaded for the bombing which killed five Americans and two Indians.
Saudi Arabia said last year it had discovered an explosives-laden car being driven from Jordan into the kingdom.
